desc: Run brute-force experiments; iterate on the exact connectivity rule until it matches brute force on all random small cases (handle multiple universal-overlap vertices and nested-clique separations)
Derive and prove the structural lemma for connected components; implement component labeling in O(N log N)
Confirm the diameter bound empirically; prove the shortest-path case enumeration (direct edge, one intermediate, two intermediates)
Implement direct-edge check: O(1) disjointness test per query
Implement common-neighbor (2-hop) minimum via prefix/suffix min arrays over sorted-by-R / sorted-by-L orders, O(1) per query
Build end-to-end verifier: current solution vs brute-force Dijkstra on random small inputs; categorize every mismatch by case (connectivity, 2-hop, 3-hop, 4-hop)
Recheck whether diameter of the main component is actually ≤ 3 (the max=4 measurement may have included isolated vertices); if ≤ 3, drop the 4-hop case entirely

Replace ad-hoc 3-hop/4-hop candidate-edge logic with a provably correct precomputation: per-vertex cheapest/second-cheapest neighbors per side with argmin, plus sweep/RMQ structures so each query is O(log N) with a complete case split (a left of b vs b left of a)
Re-verify connectivity labeling edge cases: N=2, all intervals identical, max L and min R from the same index
Finalize full Python solution with fast I/O; validate against samples and brute force on random small tests
